reader.title: Socorro triple hanging (1881)
bases: The item describes a 'party of lynchers' hanging a robber and then two of its own members after a mock trial (A2, A4, A11).

As printed, a lynching party hanged a man called a robber and then two of its members after an 'improvised court' convicted them of riding stolen horses, which meets the definition (A2, A4). The verdict is held at probable because the only source is an undated, unnamed wire filler item, one version of which ran in a humor column with a joke ending (A11).
Every copy repeats one of two wordings of a single wire item with no date, names or local confirmation, and the Pinal Drill rewrite places it in Texas (A2, A4, A11).

summary.text: The Socorro triple hanging was the reported hanging of three unnamed men by a "party of lynchers" at Socorro, New Mexico, in late October or early November 1881.
According to a widely reprinted wire item, the lynchers hanged a man described as a robber and then two of their own members, whom they found riding stolen horses.
The papers treated it as a curiosity of frontier justice, and one Arizona paper printed it as a joke.
In the longer version of the item, a "lynching party met at Socorro, New Mexico, a few days ago to hang a robber."
After the hanging, "before the meeting adjourned," the party found that two of its members were "mounted on stolen horses."
The two men were "arrested and brought before an improvised court," and within minutes they were hanged "alongside of the first victim."
The shorter version says only that "an immediate trial resulted in conviction, and two more bodies were quickly suspended."
No copy names any of the three men or the lynchers, gives a date or place of the hangings, or states anyone's race.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.
The item reached readers as filler among unrelated short news.
The Shenandoah Herald of Woodstock, Virginia, carried the short version on 2 November, and the Lancaster Daily Intelligencer printed the longer one on 4 November under "News of the Day."
Papers in New Jersey, Maine, Pennsylvania and Tennessee reprinted one wording or the other without comment through 25 November, and one Pennsylvania copy misspelled the town as "Sorocro."
On 24 December the Pinal Drill of Pinal City, Arizona Territory, rewrote the story for its "All Sorts" humor column.
Its version had the lynchers ride "out from Socorro, Texas" and closed with the quip that "tbe demands of justice had been fully met" and that further hangings would leave no one to tell the tale.
No New Mexico paper in the coverage reports the episode.
The early wire copies place the hangings at Socorro, New Mexico, while the later Pinal Drill rewrite puts them in Texas.
The wire copies call the first victim "a robber," but the Pinal Drill describes him as a man the lynchers "suspected of robbery."

accounts.label: Short wire item
accounts.gist: Lynchers who had hanged a robber at Socorro, New Mexico, found two of their number on stolen horses; an immediate trial convicted them and 'two more bodies were quickly suspended.'

accounts.label: Longer wire item
accounts.gist: A lynching party met at Socorro 'a few days ago' to hang a robber; before adjourning it found two members on stolen horses, arrested them, tried them before an improvised court and hanged them beside the first victim.

accounts.label: Pinal Drill rewrite
accounts.gist: Lynchers rode out from 'Socorro, Texas' and hanged a man suspected of robbery, then two of their own; it closes with a quip that the hangings stopped so someone would be left to tell the story.

framing.detail: Eastern and Southern weeklies and dailies ran the item without comment among unrelated short news items (A2, A4); it was reprinted at least through late November.
The Pinal Drill printed it in an 'All Sorts' humor column and added that 'the demands of justice had been fully met', treating it as a joke.

conflicts.note: The Texas placement appears only in a late, rewritten humor-column version; the earlier wire copies say New Mexico.

versions.value: 'a man whom they suspected of robbery'

conflicts.note: Wording differs in the rewrite; no source gives particulars of the robbery.

record_check.dossier: No copy says any victim was taken from officers; the two horse riders were 'arrested' by the lynching party itself
Race of the three men is not stated in any copy; nothing ties the episode to anti-Black violence
First man accused of robbery; the other two accused of riding stolen horses
Three hanged, as reported in a single unverified wire item

info: Undated; 'a few days ago' in early-November copies, so before 2 November 1881 (earliest copy)
Socorro, New Mexico (most copies); 'Socorro, Texas' in one rewrite
Three unnamed men: a 'robber' and two members of the lynching party; race not stated
First man called 'a robber' (A2, A4) or 'suspected of robbery' (A11); the other two were found 'mounted on stolen horses'
